snug — what this sandbox would be. Nothing was started.

The project directory, writable from inside:
  /home/u/proj/sub
Your home directory:
  /home/u
Both keep the exact path they have on your host. snug never relocates a path,
because a tool that prints an absolute path inside should print one that means
the same thing outside.

Selected profiles:
  @sys @home @cwd-rw @podman-socket
A profile only ever GRANTS. There is no rule anywhere that takes something
away, so adding a profile can only ever make the sandbox see more, and the way
to see less is to select fewer.

FILESYSTEM
  The root is an empty tmpfs. It has 10 paths read-only, 11 writable, and
  1 file snug generates itself rather than binding from your host.
  Everything else on this machine is not missing by a rule — it was never
  granted, so there is nothing there to deny.

  Writable, which is the half worth reading twice:
    /dev
    /home/u
    /home/u/.cache
    /home/u/.config
    /home/u/.local
    /home/u/.local/share
    /home/u/.local/state
    /home/u/proj
    /home/u/proj/sub
    /proc
    /tmp

WHAT IS NOT IN HERE
  No X11 and no Wayland: a GUI program will not open a window, and nothing
  inside can read your screen or your keystrokes.
  No D-Bus, session or system. No host abstract sockets of any kind.
  No host loopback. A service you are running on 127.0.0.1 is unreachable
  from inside, under every profile, including the networked ones.
  No ~/.ssh. Your private keys are not in this filesystem at all.
  No root, no setuid, and no process snug did not start — everything here
  dies with the sandbox.

NETWORK
  None. The sandbox has its own empty network namespace with nothing in it
  but loopback, and no helper process to carry packets anywhere. This is
  the absence of a network profile rather than a setting, so it cannot be
  switched back on by accident.

CONTAINERS
  There is a real container engine for this run, and it is snug's own — a
  sibling process, not the host's podman and not something inside the sandbox.
  What the sandbox talks to is a filtering proxy: a request that would change
  state and that the filter has not read is refused rather than forwarded.
  The engine sees a view DERIVED from this policy, not your host tree.
  This run therefore starts a stage process even with no network profile: the
  engine needs the stage for its user namespace, not for the network.
  A container gets the sandbox's network, which here is no network. It also
  means `podman run -p 8080:80` publishes nothing your host can reach.

COMMAND
  /bin/sh

This is the summary. `snug --dry-run` has the complete list — every mount, every
environment variable, the bwrap argv — and is the screen to read when you are
checking snug rather than orienting yourself.
